mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a financial crisis.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate pricing power, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) of more than 10% month-over-month, combined with a rising CPI, signals a housing-driven demand boom that temporarily boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.3% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in the same month signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases uncertainty and risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < -0.2% AND CPIAUCSL < -0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in Real Personal Income (implied by GDPC1 and RSAFS dynamics) signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for equities-sensitive goods and services, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline for two consecutive months
regime_hint: weak demand environment outside of recession
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
